questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of not more than 300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** Students in your school continue to neglect English. Write an article in your school magazine convincing them not to neglect English anymore, and to consider its importance.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC sanctionne autant le respect du format imposé (article de magazine scolaire, essai d'opinion, essai argumentatif de type « Discuss ») que le contenu. Un article de magazine scolaire s'adresse à un lectorat de camarades, avec un titre accrocheur et un ton engageant ; un essai sur « The future of X » développe une réflexion prospective structurée en plusieurs scénarios ou arguments ; un sujet de type « Discuss » exige impérativement d'examiner le pour et le contre avant de conclure, jamais une défense unilatérale d'un seul point de vue. Comme le sujet propose un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les trois modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun l'un des formats possibles.

## Topic 1 - School magazine article (modèle, environ 270 mots)

**Why English Still Matters, Even Here**

By a concerned student

Walk around our school at break time and you will hear complaints about English homework long before you hear anyone actually practising the language. Many of us treat English as a subject to survive rather than a skill to master, and I believe this attitude will cost us more than a bad grade.

English is not simply another item on our timetable. It is the language of most university textbooks we will use after the BAC, the language of the internet resources we consult every day, and increasingly the language required in job interviews, even in French-speaking regions of our own country. Neglecting it now does not make it disappear from our future; it only means we will have to catch up later, under far more pressure than we face today.

Some of us assume that since we live in a French-speaking town, English will never really be useful. But look at how many opportunities, scholarships and international exchange programmes require a good level of English to even apply. Turning away from the language today quietly closes doors we have not yet noticed we might want to open.

The good news is that improving does not require extraordinary effort: reading a short English article a week, watching a film in its original version, or simply speaking more in English class instead of switching back to French at the first difficulty, would already make a real difference over a school year.

I am not asking anyone to become fluent overnight. I am asking that we stop treating English as an obstacle and start treating it as a tool that we are lucky enough to be handed for free, in school, before we ever really need it.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of not more than 300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** The future of human rights.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Opinion essay (modèle, environ 260 mots)

The future of human rights will not be decided by the documents that already protect them, but by how consistently those documents are enforced, especially against the powerful.

On one hand, there are real reasons for optimism. International cooperation on human rights has grown steadily since the middle of the twentieth century, with courts, tribunals and organisations now able to investigate abuses that used to go entirely unpunished. The case of a former head of state being arrested abroad for crimes committed at home, once unthinkable, has already happened and shows that impunity is no longer guaranteed simply because someone once held power.

On the other hand, serious obstacles remain. Many governments still violate the rights of their own citizens with little fear of consequences, particularly when they are shielded by powerful allies or vast natural resources that make other nations reluctant to intervene. Technology, too, cuts both ways: it can expose abuses to a global audience within minutes, but it also gives authoritarian governments new tools for surveillance and repression.

I believe the future of human rights depends less on writing new laws than on building the political will to apply the ones that already exist, everywhere and against everyone, not only against weak or isolated states. Ordinary citizens, informed and connected as never before, have a real role to play in keeping that pressure alive.

If this pressure continues to grow, human rights will likely become harder to violate quietly. If it fades, the progress made so far could just as easily be reversed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of not more than 300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** Natural disasters are divine messages. Discuss.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Discussion essay (modèle, environ 280 mots)

Some people believe that natural disasters such as earthquakes, floods and droughts are divine messages, warnings or punishments sent to correct human behaviour. Others see them purely as natural phenomena that science can explain without any need for divine intervention. Both views deserve careful examination.

Those who see disasters as divine messages often point to their timing or scale, which can feel too dramatic to be mere coincidence, especially when they strike communities already engaged in what some consider immoral behaviour. This interpretation offers comfort and meaning in the face of suffering that would otherwise seem entirely random and unjust.

However, this view struggles to explain why natural disasters strike indiscriminately, affecting devout communities and irreligious ones, children and adults, the innocent and the guilty, without any visible pattern related to behaviour. Science, meanwhile, offers a coherent explanation: earthquakes result from the movement of tectonic plates, floods from excessive rainfall or poor drainage systems, and droughts from long-term climate patterns; none of these mechanisms shows any relationship to human morality.

I believe treating natural disasters purely as divine punishment can be dangerous, because it may discourage the practical measures, such as early warning systems, better construction standards and environmental protection, that actually reduce human suffering when disasters strike. A community convinced that a flood is solely a divine message may invest in prayer where it should also invest in stronger river defences.

Natural disasters can certainly be interpreted as moments to reflect on how we live, on our relationship with the environment and with each other. But treating them strictly as divine messages, rather than natural events we can prepare for and mitigate, risks costing more lives than it saves.

### Piège à éviter
Sur un sujet de type « Discuss », rédiger uniquement un plaidoyer en faveur d'une seule thèse (par exemple défendre uniquement l'origine divine, ou uniquement l'explication scientifique) est sanctionné : la consigne exige explicitement d'examiner les deux points de vue avant de conclure.

### Conseil
Pour un sujet « Discuss », prévois toujours un plan en trois temps au brouillon avant de rédiger : un paragraphe pour la thèse, un paragraphe pour l'antithèse, puis une prise de position personnelle argumentée en conclusion. Cette structure simple garantit de ne jamais oublier l'un des deux points de vue attendus.

incertitudes: Le sujet propose un choix entre trois formats différents dont un seul doit être traité le jour de l'examen ; les trois modèles fournis illustrent chacun un choix possible pour couvrir l'ensemble du barème.
